subject: E-Commerce
title: The Carbon Cost of Free Returns
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Carbon Cost of Free Returns usable.

hook.text: Free returns generate 24 million tons of CO2 annually. Each returned package travels an average of 1,000 miles back.

buildup.text: Free returns became the standard for e-commerce. Zappos proved they drive buying confidence and increase orders.

discovery.text: Many returned items are never resold. 25% of returned products end up in landfills because reprocessing costs more.

twist.text: Zara and H&M started charging for returns by mail. The free return era may be ending as costs become unsustainable.

climax.text: Free returns fueled e-commerce growth but created an environmental disaster. The hidden cost was always the planet.

punchline.text: 24M tons of CO2, 25% to landfill. Free returns grew e-commerce and waste.

quiz.question: What happens to 25% of returned e-commerce products?
options: They end up in landfills because reprocessing costs more than the item is worth
